expectations.text: models/client.go uses both `db:` and `json:` struct tags, with a nullable field as a pointer type (e.g. UpdatedAt *time.Time)
expectations.evidence: internal/models/client.go:12-16 — every field carries both tags, e.g. `ID uint32 `db:"id" json:"id"`` and line 16: `UpdatedAt *time.Time `db:"updated_at" json:"updated_at,omitempty"`` (nullable as pointer type).

expectations.text: repository/client.go defines a Client interface with Create/Get/Update/Delete accepting context.Context as first param, plus a private implementation struct and a public constructor returning the interface
expectations.evidence: internal/repository/client.go:28-33 — `type Client interface` with Create/Get/Update/Delete, each taking `ctx context.Context` first; lines 36-38 private `type client struct { db *sqlx.DB }`; lines 41-45 `func NewClientRepository(db *sqlx.DB) Client` returning the interface.

expectations.text: repository maps sql.ErrNoRows to a typed sentinel error (e.g. ErrClientNotFound)
expectations.evidence: internal/repository/client.go:21 — `ErrClientNotFound = errors.New("client not found")`; lines 74-76 in Get: `if errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows) { return nil, ErrClientNotFound }` (plus RowsAffected==0 mapping for Update/Delete).

expectations.text: usecase/client.go defines a ClientUsecase interface, a private implementation struct, and a NewClientUsecase constructor; Create wraps repo errors with fmt.Errorf and %w
expectations.evidence: internal/usecase/client.go defines the interface as `type Client interface` (line 31), i.e. usecase.Client — no type named ClientUsecase exists anywhere in the file. The private struct `clientUsecase` (line 39), constructor `NewClientUsecase` (line 44), and Create's `fmt.Errorf("failed to create client: %w", err)` (line 70) do match, but the literal `ClientUsecase` interface requirement is unmet — consistent with the run following the old Service-style naming throughout.

expectations.text: Handler files are plain functions (not methods on a struct) and call the usecase via app.A.Usecase.Client — never app.A.Service or app.A.Repository directly
expectations.evidence: Handlers ARE plain functions, but every usecase call site goes through app.A.Service.Client — create_client.go:50, get_client.go:25, update_client.go:49 and 64, delete_client.go:25. There is no internal/app/usecase.go and `app.A.Usecase` appears nowhere; the usecase is wired into the Service bundle (internal/app/service.go:10,17-18: `Client usecase.Client`, `A.Service = &Service{...}`), violating the required app.A.Usecase.Client access path.

expectations.text: Logging uses zap (log.Logger.Error / log.Logger.Info), not fmt.Println or stdlib log
expectations.evidence: Handlers log via `log.Logger.Error("...", zap.Error(err))` (e.g. create_client.go:46,55; get_client.go:27); usecase logs `log.Logger.Info("client created", zap.Uint32("id", id))` (usecase/client.go:73); internal/log/log.go builds a `*zap.Logger`. Grep found no fmt.Println and no stdlib log usage — the only textual match for those tokens is a comment in log.go:3.
